newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities, Bechtel form water company.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities, Bechtel form water company.

text.p: North West Water, a unit of Britain's United Utilities, said on Thursday that it was setting up a new international water company with U.S. partner Bechtel Group Inc to focus on projects outside the UK and U.S.

"The joint venture will initially focus on water and wastewater projects in Asia-Pacific and Latin American regions, in addition to selected assignments in Europe and the Middle East," the companies said in a statement released in London.

North West Water, one of the world's largest private-sector water companies, and San Francisco-based Bechtel, a development, engineering, construction and project management giant, said the new company would be called International Water Ltd.
It will develop, finance, build, own and operate water and wastewater treatment plants.

Water and wastewater projects in the U.S. will be implemented through another company called U.S. Water, a separate subsidiary that is jointly owned by United Utilities and United Infrastructure Company, part of the Bechtel empire.
Gordon Waters, the managing director of the international division of United Utilities, said water projects were the biggest worldwide market after power generation.
"While people can live without electricity, everyone has to have water," he said. "And as the world's population increases, the demand for clean water is only going to become more acute."

The North West Water/Bechtel alliance, announced in 1994, sealed its first project last week -- a 45 million stg award to finance, design, build and operate 10 water treatment plants for the South Australian government.
